newsitem.title: CANADA: High activity, new interest boost Precision.
newsitem.headline: High activity, new interest boost Precision.

text.p: Brisk oil and gas drilling activity in western Canada and better recognition among U.S. portfolio managers have propeled Precision Drilling Corp shares to all-time highs over the past two weeks, an industry analyst said on Monday.

Shares in Precision, Canada's biggest drilling firm and a recognized technology leader, jumped to C$48.50 in Toronto last week from C$41.40 on December 17. On Monday, Precision shares were off C$0.65 to C$47.85.
Its shares in New York were down 5/8 to 34-3/4 on Monday.

Investors have realized the buoyant Canadian oil and gas industry has driven up demand for rigs in the market, with some experts forecasting 12,000 wells will be drilled in 1997, said Schroder Wertheim analyst James Stone.
With the exeception of the holiday season, when drilling historically drops off, well over 400 rigs have been active in Western Canada for several weeks.
Much of the activity has been attributed to the recovery in natural gas prices late this year, especially in western North America.
"There's a realization that the market is very tight," Stone said.
He also said Precision, which was listed on the New York Stock Exchange last month, has underperformed similar firms in the United States.
But some U.S. investment houses, including Schroder Wertheim and Raymond James, recently started coverage of the company, which has put more information into the hands of portfolio managers.

"The stock basically did nothing in the month following the U.S. listing. What you're seeing now, to some extent, is finally playing catch-up with the rest of the group," he said, adding he believed the stock remained undervalued.

Stone said several factors continued to bode well for Precision, including a strengthened asset base with its growing equity interest in Lynx Energy Services Corp, and high demand for its hi-tech -- and high return -- slant drilling rigs.

"Where they're going to be focusing their efforts in terms of new equipment is going to be largely in slant rigs and the profitability of that slant equipment is much greater than conventional rigs," he said.
